<p>Power is how fast energy flows (kW); energy is how much has flowed (kWh = kW × hours). A 1.5 kW hair dryer for 10 minutes and a 0.05 kW laptop for 5 hours both use 0.25 kWh.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you switch a home's appliances on and off, place these amounts on a ladder of units, and test a wind-farm claim.</p>

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

::: {.lx-lede}
[Lesson 0](00-grid-operator.qmd) used both units without stopping on them: MW on every plant, MWh in the peaker question. Here they come apart.
:::

```{=html}
<div id="t1-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Power (kW)</dt><dd>How fast energy flows, right now: the flow from a tap.</dd>
<dt>Energy (kWh)</dt><dd>How much has flowed over a stretch of time: the water in the tub.</dd>
<dt>Energy = power × time</dt><dd>1.5 kW for 10 minutes and 0.05 kW for 5 hours both give 0.25 kWh.</dd>
<dt>A ladder of ×1,000</dt><dd>Wh, kWh, MWh, GWh, TWh: from a phone charge to a nation's year.</dd>
<dt>Average and peak</dt><dd>The U.S. averaged about 479 GW in 2025. In one grid, the Southwest Power Pool, the 2025 peak hour needed about 1.6 times its average.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Energy is the area under the power curve</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

When power changes in steps, energy is the sum of power times duration over the steps, in kWh when power is in kW and time in hours:

$$E = \sum_i P_i\,\Delta t_i .$$

The two jobs: $1.5\ \text{kW} \times \tfrac{10}{60}\ \text{h} = 0.25\ \text{kWh}$ and $0.05\ \text{kW} \times 5\ \text{h} = 0.25\ \text{kWh}$. Same area, very different shapes: a tall thin block and a long low one in the top panel of your chart.

Going the other way, average power is energy divided by time, $\bar P = E / T$. For the U.S. in 2025: $4{,}200\ \text{TWh} \div 8{,}760\ \text{h} \approx 479\ \text{GW}$.

Peak against average needs one data set. The Southwest Power Pool used 298.6 TWh in 2025, an average of 34.1 GW; its peak hour needed 54.4 GW, about 1.6 times the average. [Lesson 2](02-demand.qmd) reads both from the hourly data.

Physicists measure energy in joules: $1\ \text{kWh} = 1{,}000\ \text{W} \times 3{,}600\ \text{s} = 3.6\ \text{MJ}$.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Time steps: where MW meets MWh in a model</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

In an hourly model a plant's output $p_t$ is in MW and each time step lasts $\Delta t = 1$ h, so its energy in hour $t$ is $p_t\,\Delta t$ MWh: the same number, which hides the units.

$$E = \sum_t p_t\,\Delta t$$

With 15-minute data $\Delta t = 0.25$ h. Leaving it out makes these energy-based terms four times too large.

Storage needs both kinds of number: MW (how fast it charges) and MWh (how much it holds); [lesson 9](09-storage.qmd) shows it. [Lesson 10](10-write-it-down.qmd) writes a whole model down.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What the board leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>Appliance powers are typical nameplate values; your own appliance's label gives its real one.</li>
<li>Many appliances cycle: a refrigerator or a heater switches on and off under its thermostat, so its average power is below its rating.</li>
<li>Devices on standby still draw a few watts, all day.</li>
<li>The board ignores losses in the home's wiring.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
:::

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="t1-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="perhour" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “My electricity meter measures kilowatts per hour.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. A <span class="lx-term" data-term="kilowatt-hour">kilowatt-hour</span> is kilowatts multiplied by hours: power kept up over time. “Per hour” would describe how fast the power itself changes.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="rating" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The appliance with the highest power rating always costs the most to run.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Cost follows energy, power × time: a 50 W laptop for 5 hours uses as much as a 1,500 W hair dryer for 10 minutes.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="wind" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A 100 MW wind farm powers 100,000 homes.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth, as stated: it divides 100 MW by 1 kW per home.</p><p>U.S. wind ran at 33.8% of its capacity in 2025. An average home bought 10,791 kWh a year (about 1,232 W on average), so the farm's yearly energy matches what about 27,400 homes buy.</p><p>That is an illustrative equivalent: on calm hours the farm makes little.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="t1">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="heater" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">A 2 kW heater runs for 3 hours. How much energy does it use?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">6 kW</li><li data-value="b">6 kWh</li><li data-value="c">0.67 kWh</li><li data-value="d">5 kWh</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>6 kWh: energy = power × time = 2 kW × 3 h. “6 kW” names a power, not an amount.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="gwh" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">Prairie Town used about 6,957 MWh on lesson 0's day. About how many GWh is that?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">0.7 GWh</li><li data-value="b">7 GWh</li><li data-value="c">70 GWh</li><li data-value="d">7,000 GWh</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>7 GWh: one GWh is 1,000 MWh, so divide by 1,000. Each rung of the ladder is a factor of 1,000.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
```

.t1-kwh li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 15em) minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 10px; align-items: center; }
.t1-kwh .lx-choice { min-height: 44px; }
.t1-kwhres { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
.t1-kwhres i { display: block; height: 10px; border-radius: 5px; background: var(--lx-wind); }
.t1-kwhres b { font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; }
.t1-ladder { display: grid; gap: 12px; }
.t1-lq { display: grid; gap: 8px; }
.t1-rungbtns { grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
.t1-rungbtns .lx-choice { justify-content: center; font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); }
.t1-rungs { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; gap: 0; border-left: 4px solid var(--lx-line-2); border-right: 4px solid var(--lx-line-2); border-radius: 4px; }
.t1-rung { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 7.5em minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 10px; align-items: center; min-height: 52px; padding: 6px 10px; border-bottom: 3px solid var(--lx-line-2); }
.t1-rung:first-child { border-top: 3px solid var(--lx-line-2); }
.t1-rung .u b { display: block; font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-size: 16px; color: var(--lx-ink); }
.t1-rung .u small { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--lx-ink-3); }
.t1-rung .items { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
.t1-rung .x { position: absolute; right: 8px; bottom: -11px; z-index: 1; font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-size: 11px; color: var(--lx-ink-3); background: var(--lx-surface); padding: 0 4px; }
.t1-lchip { display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: 2px 6px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 9px; background: var(--lx-good-soft); font-size: 13px; color: var(--lx-ink); }
.t1-lchip.late { background: var(--lx-warn-soft); }
.t1-lchip b { font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-weight: 600; }
.t1-wind { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.4fr) minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 14px; align-items: center; }
.t1-wind-ctl { display: grid; gap: 12px; }
.t1-wind-ctl > .lx-btn { justify-self: start; }
.t1-wind-out { border: 1px solid var(--lx-line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px; display: grid; gap: 6px; background: var(--lx-surface-2); }
.t1-wind-out .v { font-size: 34px; }
.t1-wind-out .sub { font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-size: 13px; color: var(--lx-ink-3); }
.t1-bath { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 300px) minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 18px; align-items: center; }
.t1-bath svg { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
.t1-num { font-family: var(--lx-f-display); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; fill: var(--lx-bg); }
.t1-bathlist { margin: 0; padding-left: 1.4rem; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.t1-bathlist li b { display: block; font-family: var(--lx-f-display); font-weight: 500; color: var(--lx-ink); }
.t1-bathlist li span { font-size: 14.5px; color: var(--lx-ink-2); }
.t1-strip { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 8px; }
.t1-strip li { border: 1px solid var(--lx-line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 10px 12px; display: grid; gap: 4px; align-content: start; background: var(--lx-surface); opacity: .8; }
.t1-strip li.here { opacity: 1; border-color: var(--lx-tier-1); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--lx-tier-1); }
.t1-strip .t { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 6px; }
.t1-strip .code { font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-size: 12px; color: var(--lx-ink-3); }
.t1-strip b { font-family: var(--lx-f-display); font-weight: 500; font-size: 15px; color: var(--lx-ink); }
.t1-strip .pw { font-family: var(--lx-f-mono); font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--lx-ink-2); }
.t1-strip .ex { font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--lx-ink-2); }
@media (max-width: 860px) { .t1-strip { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } .t1-bath { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } .t1-bath svg { max-width: 300px; } }
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .t1-devs { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
  .t1-meters, .t1-wind, .t1-units { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
  .t1-units dd { margin-bottom: 4px; }
  .t1-kwh li { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 4px; }
  .t1-rungbtns { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
  .t1-rung { grid-template-columns: 5.6em minmax(0, 1fr); }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .t1-logbar i, .t1-tub i { transition: none; } }
</style>
<script src="../assets/learn/learn.js" defer></script>
